name: Should accessible bathroom remodeling include a floating vanity?

mainEntity.name: Does a wall-mounted vanity actually help with accessibility, or is it just a design trend?
mainEntity.text: Does a wall-mounted vanity actually help with accessibility, or is it just a design trend?

acceptedAnswer.text: A floating vanity can be a real accessibility upgrade, not just a style choice. By keeping the floor visible and open underneath, it can help wheelchair users or people with limited mobility approach the sink more easily. It also makes the room feel larger and easier to clean, which is valuable in smaller bathrooms. The tradeoff is storage space, so the design must balance access and function. The sink height, faucet reach, and plumbing placement all need to be set carefully so the vanity does not create new barriers. In a luxury remodel, a wall-mounted vanity can look very polished while still serving a practical accessibility goal. It works especially well when paired with broader circulation paths and good lighting.
acceptedAnswer.description: A floating vanity can improve accessibility by creating knee clearance and making the floor easier to navigate and clean. It works best when the sink height, trap location, and storage needs are planned so the vanity remains practical, not just decorative.
